You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Finance and support pulled the same archived orders through the supported execution modes and got different totals. Repair the system under `/app` so equivalent modes produce the same correct rows and totals for archived stores and newly ingested stores. The disagreement appears on archived mixed-generation stores that carry incomplete markers and varied origin lanes across selective reads and batch execution. Keep selective reads and batch execution working on the healthy cases. Both fast paths stay in use.

Rebuild with `/app/tools/build-all`. For the bundled drill, run `/app/bin/loam audit /app/data/cases /app/output/audit.json`; the same command accepts another case directory and report path. It writes UTF-8 JSON with top-level status set to complete, cases, and digest. Each entry in cases keeps case_id, row_count, sum_amount, pages_total, pages_read, path, and skipping as the existing per-case answer and work counters. The grading reference for those keys is `/app/docs/report-schema.md`. Answers and report bytes stay identical across repeated runs.

Fresh inputs use `/app/bin/loam ingest <CSV> <store-directory>`, which writes `<store-directory>/data.store`, and then follow the same contract. Fresh stores must record faithful live-value markers: low and high cover only live amounts, and has_absent is set when any non-live entry is present. The archived mixed-generation stores must remain readable without rewriting them. Keep the work offline and leave the healthy cases' answers and fast-path behavior unchanged.

# Audit Report Schema

The audit report is UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline. Top-level keys:

- `status`: always the string `complete`.
- `cases`: array of per-case objects (sorted by `case_id`).
- `digest`: SHA-256 over the canonical serialization of `cases` (see below).

Each case object has exactly these keys:

- `case_id` (string): directory name of the case.
- `row_count` (integer): number of live rows contributing to the sum.
- `sum_amount` (integer): sum of live amounts.
- `pages_total` (integer): number of pages in the store.
- `pages_read` (integer): number of pages actually read during the audit.
- `path` (string): absolute path to the case's `data.store`.
- `skipping` (boolean): whether the fast path skipped any pages.

Canonical serialization for the digest:

- Serialize `cases` as compact JSON (no spaces), keys in the order above.
- Encode as UTF-8 and hash with SHA-256; store the hex digest.
